symmetry_factor_note: full sphere / modelled wedge: 8 for an octant model, 1 for a full sphere. Written by the extractor from the shell grid it actually used

field_provenance.t: d3plot global timesteps, converted by the deck's time unit
field_provenance.x: cell centroid radius; ALE mesh, computed once and state-independent
field_provenance.rho: per-material ALE group mass / (alpha_m * cell_volume), using the d3plot per-material mass columns; pure-medium shell density is sum(m_m) / sum(alpha_m V). The mixture-density history column is retained in RawFrame.density but is not substituted for a material density
field_provenance.u: node velocity averaged per cell, projected on the radial direction
field_provenance.P: negative trace of the solid element stress (strengthless: sigma = -p I)
field_provenance.e: RECONSTRUCTED, not an LS-DYNA output: this d3plot carries no solid-element internal energy, so e = (p - p_cold(V))/(omega rho_m) for products and e = p/((gamma-1) rho_m) for air, where rho_m is the per-material mass/(alpha V) density, inverted per CELL and then volume-weighted onto the shells. The inverse always exists; cells where it comes out non-positive are not in a valid state of that EOS (p below the JWL cold curve, i.e. the explosive has not released its chemical energy yet) and get no energy label

material_phase_source: material_phase is fixed from the ALE volume fraction only (0 product >=95%, 1 pure air <=5%, 2 mixed); it is written before any shock-supervision withdrawal and is not changed by shock_has_supervision
material_partition_source_note: ALE material volume fraction read from the d3plot history variables, summed over the explosive parts; pure product alpha >= 0.95, pure air alpha <= 0.05, the mixed band is excluded from every label
state_validity_source: per cell: (rho, p) must be a state of the declared EOS with e > 0. contaminated_shell_fraction is the all-medium volume fraction and keeps the legacy consumer behaviour. The contribution-weighted split is written as air_contaminated_shell_fraction and product_contaminated_shell_fraction: each is the invalid contribution divided by that medium's occupied volume, so a cell that carries no weight in a medium's average cannot veto that medium's fields. Shell averaging skips nan silently; the missing contribution is therefore measured separately and air_missing_contribution invalidates pressure/energy, not density/velocity
pressure_source: negative trace of the solid-element stress, p = -(sxx+syy+szz)/3; absolute (the undeformed ambient air reads 101320 Pa at t=0); no artificial-viscosity correction is claimed

lasso_history_allocation_fix_log.reason: reproduced: neiph=22 with has_element_strain and has_solid_shell_plastic_strain_tensor both true, so the header arithmetic pre-allocates 10 while the state block carries the same 16 history columns as the 50 mm case

ale_material_mapping.note: the ALE material index is the card order, NOT part_id - 1; the volume-fraction column for ALE material k is column k

n_states_source: lasso state-count probe + boundary verification (lasso-python 2.0.3); file count 783 differs by 1

state_invalid_cells_by_phase_per_frame.note: pure-product (alpha>=0.95), pure-air (alpha<=0.05) and mixed cells are disjoint by the volume-fraction masks. An invalid product cell therefore cannot contribute weight to the air average, and vice versa; mixed cells contribute to neither pure-medium average.

cell_geometry: computed once (Eulerian mesh: node positions are state-independent)

air_native_resolution_fallback.source: first pure-air shell strictly outside the contact; original-mesh cell thickness at that shell. It is air-side, not product-side, and is only usable where the applicability flag is true.

training_location_mask.definition: material/withdrawal/contamination/front-protection position eligibility, BEFORE intersection with rho/u/e/p joint finiteness; it does not include boundary_air_location_valid
training_location_mask.field_rule: final supervision for each field = training_location_valid & field_valid_<field> & [contact.raw, R_b]
training_location_mask.legacy_valid_note: material.npz 'valid' remains the old joint four-field finite mask; it is not the training position mask

air_supervision.definition: contact_air / R_c~R_b air eligibility: material_phase==1 (ALE volume fraction only), non-empty shell, outside the contact mixing band and its protective band. It deliberately does NOT apply the legacy 'no confirmed shock -> withdraw the whole air side' rule and does NOT apply product-cell contamination to the air average.
air_supervision.field_rule: density/velocity = air location & finite (and rho>0); pressure/energy also require no missing air contribution, because a non-positive air EOS state participates in those averages with a non-positive value
air_supervision.contamination_scope: air_contaminated_shell_fraction is the invalid air contribution divided by the air-occupied volume (the same weight shell_average(AIR) uses). product_contaminated_shell_fraction is the analogous product quantity. The old contaminated_shell_fraction remains the all-medium measure for the legacy consumers and is not used to veto air fields here.
air_supervision.coverage: coverage_air is written per shell; the consumer applies min_air_coverage and records shells rejected by that threshold
air_supervision.shock_status_policy: shock_status / shock_has_supervision are recorded separately and are NOT used to withdraw air eligibility. An unconfirmed candidate shock does not delete otherwise reliable outer air.

boundary_air_field_access.purpose: outer pure-air shells are unlabelled for training but keep their shell-averaged fields so R_b detection can verify an ambient state; material==2 alone is never treated as environmental proof

resolution_note: shells finer than the ALE cell spacing near the charge are empty by construction: a shell with no cell centroid in it has no state to average. empty_shell_fraction measures that mismatch; those shells are marked invalid

front_detection.contact: per-frame geometric reconstruction (section 9): a spherically symmetric PLIC cut of the all-cell volume-weighted product fraction. The interface radius in a shell [a, b] with fraction alpha solves (r^3 - a^3)/(b^3 - a^3) = alpha, so the cut reproduces the cell phase volume by construction and the round-off is reported per frame. The position is the outer bound of the mixing band when the band spans more than one shell. It is NOT the alpha = 0.5 shell crossing any more: that crossing is kept separately as contact_shell_crossing_radius_m, purely as an auxiliary cross-check, because the shell average smears the interface over about one shell. When the reconstruction cannot locate the interface it returns no radius at all and the reason is recorded in contact_reconstruction_reason; a bracket is always reported.
front_detection.shock: OUTER EDGE OF THE CONTIGUOUS OVER-PRESSURE RUN attached to the contact, air side only (alpha < 0.5), threshold = ambient x (1 + 1e-2), edge linearly interpolated. NOT 'the outermost over-threshold shell': the far-field pressure is numerical noise around p/p_amb = 1.000 with excursions up to ~1.5%, so the outermost rule locks onto a noise spike tens of millimetres beyond the shock and moves by 5-8 mm between 2500 and 5000 shells. See shock_status_counts and shock_rh_* for why a front when it is
front_detection.method: pressure-gradient candidates on contiguous valid air-side shells, then RH verification against the measured two-sided states; the shock speed comes from mass conservation and is therefore NOT independent evidence
front_detection.tolerance_basis: the RH tolerances are uniform-normalised residuals, NOT the loose tolerances quoted for states inside a numerically smeared wave; they are re-checked against this project's baseline and resolution

contact.rule: eligible only when the geometric reconstruction located the interface inside a mixing band bracketed by the expected phases, or exactly on a shared face, and the band spans no empty shell

shock.rule: eligible only for confirmed candidates, which is where a reliable radius range exists

front_supervision_eligibility.note: the two fronts are independent: an ineligible shock never removes a usable contact label, and vice versa

contact_initial_offset_note: at t = 0 the contact surface is at R_0 by definition, so both numbers are direct, model-free error readings of the two locators on the same frame. The geometric reconstruction is the one carried in contact_radius; the shell crossing is kept only as the auxiliary cross-check (section 9)

contact_resolution.0: NOT DETECTED: the geometric reconstruction could not locate the interface, so contact_radius is nan. The bracket is still valid and the reason is in contact_reconstruction_reason
contact_resolution.1: SUB-CELL: a reconstruction exists but is not eligible as a label — the mixing band is not bracketed by the expected phases, or it spans an empty shell. contact_empty_shells_in_gap counts the latter
contact_resolution.2: resolved: the interface was located with both neighbours confirmed

mesh_resolution_note: The ALE element radial thickness is the resolution floor for every front position and for h = R_s - R_c. Measured on the 50 mm case it is ~0.85 mm inside the charge but 9.7-12.7 mm in the 50-60 mm air, 31 mm at 90-120 mm and 105 mm beyond 3 m. Refining the SHELL grid does not change it: the shell grid only resamples a coarse cell. Two quantities are therefore reported separately: the shell-grid convergence (2500 vs 5000 shells, differences relative to R_0 / R_s / h) and the mesh floor from shock_cell_thickness_m.
initial_detonation_check: The contact radius at t = 0 is R_0 by construction, so its measured value is a free calibration of the whole front-location chain. See contact_initial_offset_m; on the 50 mm case the measured value is ~2 mm high, which is about a third of the first air cell's 10 mm radial thickness.
time_origin: t is the raw LS-DYNA physical time; t_0 is the first extracted state
